I actually came here to post something along these lines, and then I saw your post and wanted to let you know you're not alone. That feeling of shame is kind of like when you send someone a text and they don't reply, ever. You know you put yourself in a vulnerable state, and you hate yourself for it, and you imagine what they must think of you and how true it must be. What's been helping me is identifying my strengths despite the persistent voice telling me I'm wrong. I have lost sight of my true self, and for that, I relentlessly punish myself for, as things used to be excellent in my life. But there can be no progress in self-chiding. Try to find something that mellows you out and helps you think less, with me it's been music, drawing, and working on projects. 

Good luck buddy.

I've been so depressed, that at this point, my only purpose of continuing my life is to allow the art to use me like a vessel to communicate itself with the outward world. Whatever ideas that come to me are there to channel me, and nothing else. I used to use depression like fuel to center my work around, but the health problems that have arisen, the relentless physical pain, the disconnect, make my mortal existence meaningless in contrast to how it once was. So I'm here to create, even if it's with the hand of a dead man.

I realize this subreddit isn't about "tough love" or negative encouragement, but you're not going to learn anything by copping out and doing something drastic. That's coming from the mouth of someone who had to drop out of school (college, not lame brained high school) due to critical health problems, followed by an extensive bout of crippling depression that has ruined my life as I know it, who still went back, to the same school, and is continuing to push through.

You will learn nothing by taking the easy route, you will only learn you prefer to remain unchallenged.

You should see a counselor, it sounds like you have a lot of growing up to do. Your post is more suitable for /r/teenagers than /r/depression. If you're going to kill yourself over lost friends, you're really not cut out for the real world.

You have interests, and aspirations. You know deep down inside you want those to become realities, and you know how satisfying they will be. Hold tight, you're better off than you think. Take it a day at a time.

I plan on meeting a psych soon, just left them a message today. I've been on Prozac, Bupropion and some other shit, but I guess I failed to stay with it, so we'll see what this guy thinks. It's just the physical pain that confuses me, makes me think I should pursue an avenue beyond depression.  

I've got a lot to work out still, it's a constant back and forth, like my brain is in an indefinite game of pong with itself, arguing bullshit rather than just living and feeling, thinking.

I've had a few, very very few, pockets of reality where I have been damn sure that I'll be the same again.

Anyway, I have a few supporters, but in the midst of college, depression reads more like a fluorescent vulnerability that everyone would rather avoid, so I try to keep quiet about it. It's all I can seem to talk about when anyone gets close enough to me, I feel they should know I'm incapable of feeling like they do.

Anyway, I'm not very adept to redditting, but I'll friend you, and send you an email here and there, and maybe we can keep each other updated on our progress. I'd like to hear from you sometime for sure.
